title: Anchor your analysis to a defined time window
when_to_use: Task involves analyzing performance or conversion metrics over a period (e.g., 'last quarter', 'monthly', 'rolling 30 days').
experience:
- Immediately after reading the task, identify the time frame required or define a reasonable, unified window (e.g., last complete month).
- Before querying, filter all source tables to this window using the appropriate timestamp column (e.g., conversation_created_at).
- Check for and handle time zone inconsistencies across date columns.
- Report the chosen time window as a parameter in your initial exploration and include it in all aggregated results.
checklist: Identify the time anchor or define one
Apply time filter to all relevant data before aggregation
Explicitly state the chosen window in outputs
common_failure_prevented: Prevents analyzing irrelevant or temporally misaligned data, ensuring metrics like monthly conversion rates are computed correctly.

title: Operationalize abstract metric definitions before computation
when_to_use: Task defines a key metric in ambiguous terms (e.g., '72-hour conversion', 'retention rate') without a precise data specification.
experience:
- Translate the metric definition into explicit SQL or code logic using available fields before any calculation.
- Validate that the required data fields exist and are populated for the defined logic.
- Create a small sample verification (e.g., count of qualifying events) to confirm the logic matches the business intent.
- Report the operational definition alongside the final metric results.
checklist: Explicitly map metric definition to data fields
Verify data availability for the logic
Test on a sample before full calculation
common_failure_prevented: Prevents misinterpretation of metrics (e.g., using stage tags instead of activity timestamps for a 72-hour usage conversion).

title: Map core analysis entities to the correct business level
when_to_use: Task requires analyzing performance for entities like 'customers' or 'companies' but data contains related entities like 'contacts' or 'conversations'.
experience:
- Identify the primary business entity (e.g., 'paying company') from the task description.
- Determine the correct table and key for that entity (e.g., company_id, monthly_spend).
- Before analysis, perform and validate the necessary join or mapping (e.g., conversation→contact→company).
- Report the mapping logic and counts (e.g., X% of conversations successfully mapped to a paying company).
checklist: Locate the correct primary key and table
common_failure_prevented: Prevents analyzing data at the wrong granularity (e.g., contact-level) when company-level metrics are required.
